one_line: Western Chalukya military commander and patron of the Mahadeva Temple at Itagi, c. 1112 CE.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, medium height, well-built but lean and disciplined
appearance.face: oval face with warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, sharp jawline, neatly trimmed moustache, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes with a steady gaze, default expression calm and resolute with a hint of quiet pride
appearance.hair: thick black hair oiled and combed back into a compact topknot secured with a simple gold band, sides neatly controlled, with a narrow folded turmeric-yellow cloth band tied around the forehead like a modest headband, no crown or elaborate helmet
appearance.costume: era-accurate Western Chalukya noble commander attire: a long-sleeved fitted cotton angiya (tunic) in deep indigo blue reaching mid-thigh, with subtle woven borders in muted gold along the collar and cuffs; over it a wrapped silk uttariya (shawl) in rich maroon draped from left shoulder across chest and back in a clean diagonal, the ends hanging to the right hip; a sturdy cream-colored cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and brought between the legs in warrior’s style, pleats falling to the ankles, with a thin dark red border; around his waist a wide leather kamarband (belt) dyed dark brown, reinforced with simple bronze studs and a central rectangular bronze buckle, from which hangs a small cloth pouch; jewelry kept dignified and plausible for a high-ranking commander—short gold chain at the neck, small circular gold earrings, and a single broad copper bangle on his right wrist; on his feet, closed leather paduka-style sandals in dark brown, strapped over the mid-foot; no extravagant armor, but a practical sleeveless quilted cotton vest in muted olive-green worn over the tunic, lightly padded and stitched in rectangular panels to suggest protection while remaining historically grounded
appearance.signature: a sheathed broad Deccan-style straight sword with a slightly flared tip, iron blade and simple disc-pommel hilt, carried at his left hip in a dark brown leather scabbard with understated bronze fittings and a small engraved sun symbol near the mouth of the scabbard

ref_desc: Mahadeva the Commander is a warm medium-brown Deccan man in his early 40s with an oval face, black topknot and turmeric-yellow headband, wearing an indigo tunic, olive quilted vest, maroon shawl, cream dhoti, dark brown belt and sandals, carrying a broad straight sword in a dark brown scabbard accented with muted gold and bronze.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Mahadeva the Commander: a dignified Western Chalukya military patron from c. 1112 CE, early 40s, medium height, lean but strong, with an oval face, warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, sharp jaw, neatly trimmed moustache and calm, resolute almond eyes. His thick black hair is oiled back into a compact topknot held by a simple gold band, with a narrow folded turmeric-yellow cloth band around his forehead. He wears a deep indigo long-sleeved fitted tunic with subtle muted-gold borders, over which sits a sleeveless olive-green quilted cotton vest stitched in rectangular panels, plus a rich maroon silk shawl draped diagonally from left shoulder to right hip. His cream cotton dhoti with a thin dark red border is wrapped tightly and falls to his ankles in clean pleats, held by a wide dark brown leather belt with bronze studs and buckle, a small pouch hanging from it. He has a short gold neck chain, small round gold earrings, and a single broad copper bangle on his right wrist, with closed dark brown leather paduka-style sandals on his feet. At his left hip, show his signature broad straight Deccan sword sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard with simple bronze fittings and a tiny engraved sun near the mouth. Use a palette dominated by indigo blue, maroon, cream, olive green, dark brown and muted gold, and present him standing neutrally with clear front view so all details of face, hair, garments and sword are visible.
